The words

So let our lips and lives express
The holy gospel we profess,
So let our works and virtues shine
To prove the doctrine all divine.

Thus shall we best proclaim abroad
The honours of our saviour God;
When the salvation reigns within,
And grace subdues the power of sin.

Our flesh and sense must be deny'd,
Passion and envy, lust and pride;
While justice, temperance, truth and love
Our inward piety approve.

Religion bears our spirits up,
While we expect that blessed hope,
The bright appearance of the Lord,
And faith stands leaning on his word.

How to sing it from the solfa

  • Find doh first. Play or hum Eb and sing d r m f s up from it, so the whole choir has the key in their ears before you start.
  • Pitch the first note. The tune starts on s (B♭), on the word “So”, as a pickup before the first full bar.
  • Count the time. 4/4 means four crotchet beats in each bar. In the grid every cell is half a crotchet: a dash (–) holds the note before it, and _ is a rest.
  • Know the notes. The tune uses d r m f s l t and the chromatic fe. A comma after a note (s,) is the octave below; an apostrophe (d') is the octave above.

About the hymn

Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book I, collected from the Scriptures, hymn 132, headed “Holiness and grace, Titus 2. 10-13”.

Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.

  • Words (1707): Isaac Watts (1674–1748)
  • Music (1782): Samuel Webbe (1740–1816)

Tune MELCOMBE by Samuel Webbe (1740–1816); words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748).

Sung to the same tune: At Thy Command, Our Dearest Lord, Awake, Our Souls, Away, Our Fears, Behold How Sinners Disagree, Bury'd in Shadows of the Night, Eternal Spirit! We Confess, From Heaven the Sinning Angels Fell, God of the Morning, at Whose Voice, Great God, to What a Glorious Height, How Vast the Treasure We Possess, In Thine Own Ways, O God of Love, My God, How Endless Is Thy Love, My God, Permit Me Not to Be, New Every Morning Is the Love, Now Let the Lord My Saviour Smile, Praise, Everlasting Praise Be Paid, Sing to the Lord That Built the Skies, This Is the Word of Truth and Love, Thou Whom My Soul Admires Above, When the Great Builder Arch'd the Skies.

Questions about So Let Our Lips and Lives Express

What is the doh of So Let Our Lips and Lives Express?

In this version, in Eb major, doh is Eb. If your choir sings it in another key, doh moves to the new key note and every solfa syllable stays the same — that is what movable doh means.

What note does So Let Our Lips and Lives Express start on?

It starts on s (B♭ in Eb major), a pickup on the word “So” before the first full bar. Find doh first, then sing up or down to s.

Is So Let Our Lips and Lives Express in the public domain?

Yes. Isaac Watts died in 1748, Samuel Webbe died in 1816; the words were first published in 1707 and the music in 1782. Everyone named died before 1955 and both were published before 1929, so the hymn is out of copyright in the UK, the EU, the United States and Nigeria. Modern arrangements and translations can still be under copyright.
